title: Farmers' Tk 10 accounts and deposits fall, central bank report shows
excerpt: Bangladesh Bank's Financial Inclusion Report 2025 puts formal access at 64.5% of adults, but government-to-person payments through mobile money fell.

image.alt: Farmers harvesting rice in a wetland field in Bangladesh
image.credit: A S M Jobaer / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0

content:
About 64.5% of adults in Bangladesh have access to formal financial services, according to Bangladesh Bank’s Financial Inclusion Report 2025, The Business Standard reported on 10 November. The report also shows falling numbers in accounts meant for farmers and in government payments through mobile money.

The gaps

  • Women hold about 42% of mobile money accounts (105.6 million of 250.2 million).
  • Girls hold 45.1% of school banking deposits, boys 54.9%.
  • Rural areas have most school banking accounts (52.24%), but urban areas hold most of the money (70.29% of deposits).
  • No-frills deposits grew mainly because of safety-net beneficiaries and very poor savers, the report found.

Why it matters

Falling balances in farmers’ and students’ accounts fit the picture of household strain in the World Bank’s latest poverty estimates. The drop in government-to-person mobile payments matters for cash transfer programmes, including the new Family Card. Microfinance NGOs and women’s economic empowerment programmes can use the gender figures to target outreach, since women still hold well under half of mobile money accounts.

Limitations

Account counts include dormant and duplicate accounts, so they overstate the number of people served. The 64.5% access figure depends on the report’s definition, which the news coverage does not set out. Devlens has not seen the full report.

Sources

  • Financial inclusion reaches 64.5% of adults, but farmers’, students’ savings decline: Cenbank report, The Business Standard, 10 November 2026
